variants.headline: {{majorityFaith}} leads in most of our cities
body: {{majorityFaith}} holds a majority in most of our cities. Our nation founded a different faith, {{founded}}.

variants.headline: Keep the faith we founded
body: People of {{founded}}, another faith, {{majorityFaith}}, leads in most of our cities. If your children can learn the words to every song in the street, they can learn the words to one prayer. Say it with them before supper, while everyone is still at the table.

variants.headline: My daughter still comes on washing day
body: Sir, you report that {{majorityFaith}} leads in most of our cities. My daughter keeps it; I keep {{founded}}. She is the only one of my children who comes round on washing day. Pray spare me the letters of condolence.

variants.headline: Who keeps the old shrine open?
body: {{majorityFaith}} has a majority in most of our cities. In the lane behind the dye works, some of its worshippers still bring oil to the shrine of {{founded}} and help patch its roof. Those families could keep the shrine open even if its congregation dwindles.

variants.headline: {{city}} takes the faith we founded
body: The majority faith of {{city}} is now {{religion}}, the creed this nation founded. The change came by conversions among the city's own people. {{city}} lies beyond the lands we neighbor, and the creed reached it anyway.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} receives the faith we founded
body: We are credibly informed that {{cityState}} has taken {{religion}}, the creed this nation founded, as its majority faith. The letters from thence relate quiet processions and altars newly swept. Whatever else divides the great powers, a shared creed gives two peoples a courteous subject of conversation.

variants.headline: Lamps in the windows at {{city}}
body: A trader passing through {{city}} told our reporter the same story twice: lamps at dusk, altars swept before market, the neighbors calling it the new custom. The majority faith of the city is now {{religion}}, the creed we founded. He sold out of candles by Thursday and gave the takings to the shrine.

variants.headline: Our faith just took a whole city-state
body: {{city}} now keeps {{religion}}, the faith we founded, as its majority creed. A whole city-state, converted, no treaty required. The creed is doing our diplomacy for us. Send the traders next.

variants.headline: Our faith reaches {{cityName}}
body: {{cityName}}, a city of {{civilization}} some {{distance}} leagues from our nearest city, has taken {{religion}}, the creed this nation founded, as its majority faith. Conversions in the city account for the change.

variants.headline: A distant city turns to our faith
body: A city far beyond our borders has taken {{religion}}, the creed this nation founded, as its majority faith. Conversions in the city account for the change, and the distance has not slowed the creed.

variants.headline: Our creed gains a distant majority
body: In {{civilization}}, {{cityName}} has taken {{religion}}, the faith we founded, as its majority creed. The nearest of our settlements lies {{distance}} tiles away on the survey map.
A sermon can reach well beyond the ground a regiment can hold. The question for both capitals is where the people of that city will turn for counsel on matters of faith.

variants.headline: They sing of a far city keeping our faith
body: They say a far city, {{distance}} days past the last road we know, has turned to {{religion}}, the faith of our own hearths. The travelers' songs give the town a new verse this year, and the verse is ours.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} deepens its faith
body: The faith {{religion}}, kept by {{civilization}}, has gained a new article of belief. Its teaching now reaches further than before, and the work was that nation's own.

variants.headline: A foreign power deepens its faith
body: The faith {{religion}}, kept by a major power abroad, has gained a new article of belief. Its teaching now reaches further than before, and the work was that power's own.

variants.headline: A creed reformed in a foreign land
body: It is set down that {{civilization}} has reformed the faith of {{religion}}, weighing its rites and setting them in order anew. Reform is a costly virtue. What the old observances held together, the new order keeps or sets aside, and the price is counted in custom.

variants.headline: Notice to readers of divinity
body: We are advised that {{civilization}} has added new articles to the faith of {{religion}}. Readers who mean to speak on the matter will wish to see the articles themselves before they venture an opinion.

variants.headline: Our faith leads in most cities of {{civilization}}
body: In {{civilization}}, {{religion}} now holds a majority in most cities. The faith was founded here.

variants.headline: Our faith gains ground abroad
body: {{religion}}, the faith founded here, now holds a majority in most of the cities of another major power.

variants.headline: Will pilgrims from {{civilization}} visit our shrines?
body: {{religion}} now holds a majority in most cities of {{civilization}}. Worshippers who know the prayers can join in when they visit our shrines. Whether our inns and stallholders see any of that business depends on how easily pilgrims can make the trip.

variants.headline: A potter's bowls for {{civilization}}
variants.byline: A Trader of the Long Roads
body: Sir, my daughter makes bowls for our shrine and has got better at it than I ever was. I read that {{religion}} now leads in most cities of {{civilization}}, so I've offered to take some of her best work on my next trip. I'd like her to meet the people who'll use it.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} founds a religion
body: A new faith has entered the world: {{religion}}, founded by {{civilization}}. It will travel with that power's traders, settlers and priests, wherever they go.

variants.headline: A new religion is founded abroad
body: A new faith has been founded by a power abroad. Its name is {{religion}}, and it will travel with its founder's people wherever they go.

variants.headline: Entered in the record: a new creed
body: Founder: {{civilization}}
Creed: {{religion}}
Holy city: {{holyCity}}
So the faith begins: a founder, a creed, a seat.

variants.headline: A new creed is on the map
body: A new creed is on the map tonight. Its name is {{religion}}. Its founder is {{civilization}}. Faith travels with settlers and traders. Where it takes hold, that power's word travels with it.

variants.headline: {{religion}} overtakes {{former}} in the tally of cities
body: {{religion}} has a majority in most of our cities. {{former}} held that distinction at the previous count.

variants.headline: {{religion}} now leads in most of our cities
body: No faith held a majority in most of our cities at the last count. {{religion}} does now.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our own faith leads the nation
body: Hear it, households of the nation! {{religion}}, the faith we founded, now has a majority in most of our cities. Ring it out where there's a bell to ring. The faith we founded leads at home!

variants.headline: A new majority, an old day of rest
body: {{religion}}, a creed founded abroad, now has a majority in most of our cities. The next change to watch is the calendar. A town can count a new majority and keep the day it has always shut its shops. That custom will be harder to keep if apprentices and their employers begin asking for different days off.

variants.headline: {{religion}} gains a majority in most cities of {{civilization}}
body: In {{civilization}}, {{religion}} now has a majority in most cities. The previous majority was held by {{former}}.

variants.headline: {{religion}} gains a majority across the border
body: In a power near our borders, {{religion}} now holds a majority in most cities. At the previous count, {{former}} did.

variants.headline: Two prayer books for a binder in {{civilization}}
body: Letters from {{civilization}} report that {{religion}} now holds a majority in most of its cities, where {{former}} lately led. A bookbinder there has two prayer books on his bench, one from each congregation. He says the customer who called first will have his book on Friday and the other will have to wait his turn.

variants.headline: Border towns: ask after the feast days
body: Across the border, {{religion}} now has a majority in most cities, where {{former}} used to lead. If you go across for the fairs, ask before you hitch up whether the old feast days still draw a crowd.

variants.headline: {{count}} neighboring cities turn to {{key}}
body: {{count}} cities among our neighbors now keep {{key}} as their majority faith. The changes are recent, and taken together they show how far the creed has walked along the border.

variants.headline: The border tally of faiths
body: Creed gaining along the border: {{key}}
Neighbor cities newly keeping it: {{count}}
Read together: the line is turning, town by town.

variants.headline: The ferryman counts the towns
body: The ferryman at the crossing counts the season by his passengers: {{count}} towns on the far side have all taken up {{key}}, and their pilgrims cross the water to see it done. 'New blessings, same fare,' he says, and poles back for another load.

variants.headline: One town, then the field
body: One town turns to {{key}}: news. {{count}} towns turn: a season. The wind that bends one stalk bends the field.

variants.headline: {{religion}} gains a new article of belief
body: The faith this nation founded, {{religion}}, has gained a new article of belief. Its teaching now reaches further than before, and the addition was made at home.

variants.headline: The state's stewardship adds to the creed
body: This paper records with pleasure that {{religion}}, the faith we founded, has been enriched with further observances. Such work does not happen of its own accord. It is directed, and the direction has been steady.

variants.headline: The rites set in order anew
body: In this season {{religion}} was reformed, its rites weighed and ordered anew by our own hand. The faithful will read purpose into the timing. The record notes only that the work is done, and done at home.

variants.headline: Hear it! The national faith is deepened
body: Hear it, households of the nation! {{religion}}, the faith we founded, has gained a new article of belief! A broader creed for the whole people! Carry it with you, from market to market!

variants.headline: Our cities keep more than one faith
body: Of our own cities, {{faithful}} keep {{founded}}, the faith this nation founded, and {{divided}} keep other creeds: {{others}}. The count is the present one.

variants.headline: A founded faith, unevenly kept
body: A nation that founds a faith ought to be able to keep it. Today {{divided}} of our cities pray in other creeds while {{faithful}} hold to {{founded}}.
The question is for the ministry: what has been spent on the shrines these past years, and where? Every foreign creed won its ground here one city at a time.

variants.headline: Madam, on the counting of divided cities
variants.byline: A Keeper of a Small Shrine
body: Madam Editor, you will print the tally of divided cities as though division were a debt to be called in. In my street the divided and the faithful share a wall, and the ladder I lend crosses it daily.
Print that too: a nation keeps {{founded}} by keeping its people, and no ledger ever prayed.

variants.headline: The tally of faiths in our cities
body: Cities keeping the founded faith, {{founded}}: {{faithful}}
Own cities keeping other creeds: {{divided}}
Creeds kept among them: {{others}}
One law over all of them, and more than one prayer under it.

variants.headline: {{religion}} leads in {{city}}
body: The majority faith of our own {{city}} is now {{religion}}, and recent conversions in the city have gone its way.

variants.headline: Good news, people of {{city}}
body: Good news, people of {{city}}! The city's conversions have gone the way of {{religion}}, the very creed this nation founded, and its majority faith besides! Keep the feast, and keep the faith.

variants.headline: A creed not of our founding leads in {{city}}
body: The majority faith of {{city}} is {{religion}}, a creed this nation did not found. Recent conversions in the city have gone its way.
What its growing following does to the city's festivals and its loyalties is the question the record will answer in time.

variants.headline: New hymns over the wall
body: The washing lines at {{city}} told it first, the old women say: ribbons at the shrine on a workday, and singing over the wall earlier than the bells. The majority faith of the city is {{religion}}, and the singing goes with it. One grandmother calls it weather. Her neighbor calls it the future.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} founds a pantheon
body: {{civilization}} has founded a pantheon, the first shape of that people's worship. What its rites ask, and how far they travel, the record will show in time.

variants.headline: They say the first altars are ours
body: They say it in the streets, and it is told from the wells: our own people have raised a pantheon. The elders speak of beginnings, and the households ask the old blessings in a new way. It is a good season to be counted among the faithful.

variants.headline: A pantheon entered in the foreign record
body: The scribes enter it thus: {{civilization}} has founded a pantheon. What it holds sacred and what it asks of its keepers are that people's own affair. The record notes the founding, and counts its followers from this day.

variants.headline: Notice to travelers: a new pantheon at {{cityName}}
body: Travelers are advised that {{civilization}} has founded a pantheon at {{cityName}}. Its first teaching goes by the name of {{belief}}. The curious may watch the rites; the devout may bow or pass by.

variants.headline: This nation has founded {{religion}}
body: This nation has founded a religion: {{religion}}. Its first followers are our own people, and its teaching begins at our own altars.

variants.headline: Hear it! A religion of our own
body: Hear it, from the shrines to the market squares! A religion is founded among us, and its name is {{religion}}! Let its shrines reach every city, and let its name carry ours down the roads!

variants.headline: What a founded faith carries with it
body: The nation has founded a religion, {{religion}}, and the act is larger than one creed. A founded faith travels with our traders, our settlers and our name, and where it takes root we are known before we arrive.
Standing among the peoples is built from such beginnings. The faith is ours. What the nation does with the reach is the question that follows.

variants.headline: A founding entered in the record
body: It is set down for the record: in this season the faith of {{religion}} was founded among our people. The entry stands among the acts of the realm, and later entries will carry what follows from it.
